- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is bullish (≥0.75) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish (≤0.25) — model often fails to recognize downward momentum, leading to lagged corrections.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model delays downward correction — true price drops faster than forecasted.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term trend reversion toward historical mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model consistently overestimates early days (1–7) and underestimates late days (24–30) — adjust for asymmetric decay in forecast accuracy.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment is high, model forecasts higher than true; if sentiment is low, model forecasts lower than true — use sentiment as a multiplier or offset for price adjustment.
